meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'the people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common Russian noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to borrow; (colloquial) to lend', paired with 'занимать'.

examples.trans: Then lend me at least some money.

examples.text: Ладно, ну займите тогда хотя бы денег.
examples.trans: Fine, then lend me at least some money.
Who took first place after all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to refuse, to turn down', paired with 'отказывать'.

examples.text: Марина, послушайте, это я вам отказал!
examples.trans: Marina, listen, I was the one who turned you down!
They turned him down in court.

examples.text: Я мерзкий? Марина, послушайте, это я вам отказал!
examples.trans: I'm disgusting? Marina, listen, I was the one who turned you down!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'look, appearance; view' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Из окна красивый вид на парк.
examples.trans: There is a nice view of the park from the window.

examples.text: Что вы имеете в виду, Клавдия Викторовна?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Klavdia Viktorovna?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слышать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to catch, hear clearly'.

examples.trans: Pretend that you did not hear properly.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет расслышать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to catch without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to be about to; to gather
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'uh-huh, yeah', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('third').

examples.trans: He lives on the third floor.

examples.text: Ты что, мафия? Ты же завхоз в третьем поколении.
examples.trans: What are you, the mafia? You're a supply manager, third generation.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'stage, phase' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Because that is a well-known stage.
Now the big housewarming stage is going to begin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спросить'.

examples.text: Вот это что такое, я вас спрашиваю!
examples.trans: What is this, I'm asking you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's go'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.
All right, let's go to our room.
